answer: Tie each agent key to its own outdoor sensor box that streams local temperature, humidity and light every hour, signed on the device. The network checks each stream against public weather stations and nearby boxes; a fake feed, or one copied to many keys, drifts from the real sky and gets caught. A farmer can't let a thousand keys wander out of one rack: each needs a box bolted somewhere real, on a walnut tree or a basalt wall, so fake identities cost actual places.
